about.title: Carlsbad Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grief doesn't follow a schedule, and neither should the pressure to act. When a family in Carlsbad loses someone to a preventable crash, a workplace accident, or another party's negligence, the practical questions arrive long before anyone feels ready for them. Public records show that in 2025, Carlsbad recorded 499 injury collisions, 682 people hurt, and 5 traffic deaths, with crashes clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. along corridors like I-5, Palomar Airport Road, Carlsbad Boulevard, and El Camino Real. Under California law, a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, and then by certain dependents or heirs. It is separate from any criminal case in San Diego County, and it must generally be filed within two years of the date of death, with a shorter window if a public entity is involved. We handle wrongful death claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before any filing is made.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general two-year limit runs from the date of death, and it is shorter when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Acting sooner protects that window.

items.title: Recovery for what was actually lost
items.desc: A civil claim can address funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. It moves forward regardless of whether criminal charges are ever filed.

items.question: If the crash happened on I-5 through Carlsbad, does that change who we file against?
items.answer: It might. Crashes on I-5 or a city street like El Camino Real can raise questions about whether a driver, an employer, or a public entity shares responsibility. When a government agency is potentially involved, California requires a claim to be filed much sooner than the standard two years, so it helps to have an attorney review the facts early.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it does not depend on a conviction or a criminal filing at all. We can move forward while the criminal matter is pending, and the two cases apply different standards of proof.

items.question: What does it cost to work with us?
items.answer: We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, which means there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. You can ask about costs directly during your first conversation.
